# Chapter One

“You didn’t count it twice,” Juniper said. “You never do.”

Corrigan’s hands were still on the rope. He hadn’t moved since the bell. “It wasn’t
the count,” he said. “It was the crate.”

She wasn’t listening. The kind of quiet that follows a bad tally had already
settled over the pier, and the particular weight of it sat in her chest like a
stone she couldn’t name. Not the ledger. Not the debt. The boy’s face.

“I’ll go back for the lantern,” she said, to nobody. “Before the season turns.”
